start: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Back again. What do you need?
first_meeting_scene: ^Narrator: A sharp-eyed woman in her mid-thirties looks up from three monitors of transaction graphs.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: You must be the FCA. Dr. Irina Volkova, Chief Technology Officer.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: A supervisory visit. Always a pleasure, I'm sure.
^Thank you for making the time, Dr. Volkova. I know a visit like this is disruptive.
^Let's be efficient. I need backend servers, transaction logs and wallet infrastructure.
^Thirty-seven papers and nearly three thousand citations. I've read some of your work.
professional_response: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I appreciate the courtesy. Most of your colleagues treat us as criminals from the first handshake.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: We run a privacy-focused exchange. That is not the same thing as an illegal one.
suspicious_response: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Supervisors usually start with paperwork. Customer checks, anti-laundering procedures. You went straight for the machines.
academic_response: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: You read my work? Most people from your side see "cryptographer" and hear "hacker".
^Dr. Irina Volkova: I built this exchange on sound principles. Zero-knowledge proofs, homomorphic encryption. Things I can defend.
academic_discussion: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: My research is about financial privacy. Governments should not be able to read every transaction a person makes.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: That is a privacy position, not a criminal one.
^Financial surveillance worries me too. I understand the principle.
^It also launders money. That's why people like me visit exchanges like this.

c-1: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Fair. Ask for what you need and I'll show you it's documented.

audit_discussion: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: So what does the FCA want to see? Our customer checks are compliant. Our monitoring meets the thresholds.

b: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Unless you are looking for something that isn't on a checklist.

hub: ^I'll need to test your password strength. What do people here actually use?
^What's the post-quantum work on your second screen?
^Let's start again, properly. Walk me through your anti-laundering procedures.
^(Let the cloner read her badge while she talks.)
^Satoshi's wing. You've a badge for it.
^There's something you need to see, Dr. Volkova.
^I'm going to stop pretending. I'm not from the FCA.

b: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Find me if you need anything else.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Alright. I'll be here.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Reasonable request for a supervisor. Here.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Fine. You'd find it on the file server in ten minutes anyway. Here.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: My own audit wordlist. Every crypto firm on earth picks from the same twenty words and bolts a year on the end.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Sixty-one per cent of our staff accounts fell to that list last time I ran it. Management's response was to stop me running it.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: I don't know you well enough to hand a visitor our credential data.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Earn a little trust first. Then we can talk about the backend.

research_topic: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Post-quantum key exchange. Lattice-based. The day a quantum computer breaks elliptic curves, every wallet on earth is readable, and I would rather we were ready than surprised.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: It's the part of this job I'm still proud of.
paperwork_topic: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: *thawing slightly* Now that's a supervisor's question.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Every flagged transaction comes to me personally. I review it, I decide, I sign it off. That part I do by the book.
discuss_badges: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: Badges. Trading floor for staff, this one for my office, executive badges for the top floor.

^Dr. Irina Volkova: *taps the lanyard at her collar* Four years round my neck. The badges are the one part of our security I'd defend. Satoshi is paranoid about doors and careless about passwords, which is exactly backwards.

b: ^You: I'll need to check your office reader as part of the visit. Can I borrow the badge?
^Dr. Irina Volkova: *unclips it* Bring it back. And don't tell facilities I handed it over, they'll write a memo about it.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: West door. Try not to judge the whiteboard.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: My badge stays on my neck for a visitor I met an hour ago. Nothing personal.
^Narrator: Her lanyard hangs open at her collar, well within a cloner's range. She'd never feel it read.

clone_badge: ^Narrator: You keep her talking about lattices and bring the cloner in your pocket within range of her lanyard.

b: ^Narrator: One pass, EM4100, a clean copy. She never noticed.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: ...anyway. You didn't come here for a lecture on elliptic curves.
^Narrator: The cloner didn't get a clean read.
^Narrator: The spare executive badge is in her top drawer, under a reader-install manual. You take it.
^Narrator: You put the fund allocation in front of her. She reads the per-cell lines, then the casualty line, then the signature.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Satoshi's Ghost. He signs the money with that name. He thinks it's funny.

exec_badge_handover: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I put the readers in on his floor. Facilities lent me a spare to do it and never asked for it back. Here.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: His wing is east of the data centre. He'll be at his desk; he always is.
show_blockchain_evidence: ^Narrator: You lay the transaction graph on her desk. Ransom money in. Exploit money in. The Initiative's budget back out. All of it through the mixer she wrote.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: *goes still* Where did you get our internal analysis?
^You flagged these transactions yourself. You already knew.
^It doesn't matter where. Read what it's paying for.

c-0: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I flagged them because they were wrong. Not because I knew what they paid for.

b: ^You: The Architect's Fund. $12.8 million still to go out to six cells, and a projection of 350 to 600 dead. You built the machine that moves it.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: *reads it twice* They costed the deaths. They put a number in a cell and moved on.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: I told myself this was about privacy. Financial freedom. Not... this.

^You: Hospital ransoms. Exploit sales. All of it laundered clean through your infrastructure.

^Dr. Irina Volkova: I told myself it was about privacy. I am finding that harder to say out loud than I used to.

reveal_identity: ^You: I'm SAFETYNET. The exchange you built is the bank for every ENTROPY cell we've met.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: *quietly* My work. Used to kill people.
^You didn't see the whole picture. You can help us take it apart.
^You built it and you profited. But cooperation is a way to make it right.

c-0: ^You: You built these systems believing in them. ENTROPY turned them into a weapon. Help us dismantle their network and that means something.
c-1: ^You: You're in this up to your neck. The honest way out is to help us end it, not to pretend you didn't know.

b: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I won't turn on Satoshi on the strength of one conversation and a graph.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Financial privacy is a right. If some people abuse it, that is on them, not on me.
^Then you're complicit, and I'm treating you as complicit.
^You wrote "What have I become?" I read it in your office.
^Think about it. I'll come back before anyone else does.

c-2: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: You're giving me time. Nobody in this building has ever done that.

notes_leverage: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: You were in my office.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: ...Yes. I wrote it, and then I went back to work, because he pays well and it was easier.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: I don't want to write it again.
recruit_accept: ^Narrator: She is quiet for a long moment.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Then I'll help you. On one condition: what I give you tonight gets used. Not buried.
^You: You'll know. You have my word.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: Then start with the mixer. The pool keys, the wallet map, and the name on the account that pays me. All of it, tonight.
^? Thank you. For treating this as a choice.
detain_irina: ^You: Dr. Irina Volkova, I'm detaining you for laundering and for facilitating terrorism. The police will take it from here.

b: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: *offers her wrists* I really did think I was building something good.
^Dr. Irina Volkova: *cold* This is exactly the state overreach we warned people about.

detain_irina: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I hope it was worth it.

b: ^Dr. Irina Volkova: I'm still here, and still yours. What do you need?
^Narrator: She sits very still at her desk, waiting for the police, and doesn't look up.

after_choice: ^Satoshi's wing. You've a badge for it.
